Recording & privacy

FocusFix is still in development. There is no public app download or study enrollment on this website. This draft describes local recording, optional accounts and the gated research features being prepared. It is not a research consent form or a published study invitation.

What recording includes

While you choose to record, FocusFix observes activity across apps: keyboard timing and delete-key events, clicks, scrolling, app-switch events, one-second mouse movement summaries, break timing and user-declared Work/Not working/Unknown context intervals and any separately enabled optional study ratings. Automatic capture can include non-work computer use.

It does not save typed text, individual letter keys, application names, window titles, URLs, screenshots or exact cursor paths. Custom break-activity labels are saved if you enter them. Detailed timing can still be sensitive; this data should not be treated as anonymous.

Your controls

On first launch, choose Enable recording or Not now. Start work begins manual capture after consent and separate macOS Input Monitoring access. Automatic recording needs its own explicit acknowledgement in Settings → Privacy & Research; existing recording consent, accounts, research sharing and OS access do not enable it. Automatic activity starts Unknown and can include non-work computer use while FocusFix runs.

Start work is optional during automatic capture and labels from now. End work returns automatic activity to Unknown; manual-only capture saves and stops. Pause recording and Quit stop capture; Resume deliberately restarts it. A user pause survives relaunch. Closing a window keeps the menu-bar app running. Optional Launch at login changes only on explicit action and cannot bypass consent or pause. Use Enable Input Monitoring explicitly for OS setup; opening Settings never grants or requests it by itself.

Five continuous idle minutes, sleep/lock or permission loss stop capture. Eligible lifecycle resume begins Unknown. Missing observations are unavailable coverage, not zero activity or non-work. Work labels and recorded computer time are not objective productivity. A notification’s “I’m not working” action labels from that action onward and keeps recording; correct an earlier bounded interval separately in history. Screen-use reminders outside declared work are a separate off-by-default choice.

Ordinary use has no survey prompts. Optional study check-ins require a new explicit choice and a complete reviewed study configuration; none is supplied. Old survey switches or research consent do not activate them. Missing/skipped answers stay missing. Detailed activity capture pauses during an explicit break; inactivity alone is not proof of a break.

Where the files stay

New-schema recordings currently stay in the app’s private sandbox on your Mac until you delete them. New-format research delivery remains disabled. Open Sessions and use Show in Finder to locate a recording, or export a copy to a folder you choose. FocusFix does not separately encrypt these files. Your backups and any exports you create may contain copies.

Deleting a session moves its local folder to Trash. Empty Trash to remove that copy; exports and backups are separate. The app does not remove those for you. Automatic recordings are retained even when short. Context corrections preserve original label provenance and do not rewrite raw activity files. Whole-folder exports may include private pseudonymous consent/account references; they contain no account credentials.

Optional accounts

Guests can use local features. Creating an account sends your email and authentication information to the configured Supabase service. Saving an account profile sends the name and photo you choose; local profiles remain on the Mac. Account identifiers, tokens and service logs support authentication and security. Signing in never opts you into research.

Optional research sharing

Research recruitment and collection remain disabled. Prepared automatic/non-work archives need a new reviewed consent scope and disposable-service qualification; old consent cannot authorize them. Sign-in or consent cannot backfill old activity. New archives remain ineligible, and long daily recordings do not bypass study upload caps. When an approved study opens, eligible adults can request to join. A researcher manually verifies and approves up to 50 total participants. Approved participants must review the current study consent and explicitly enable sharing before new completed recordings upload to private Supabase storage. Names and photos are excluded from recording archives, but the service can associate recordings with your account. Detailed behavioral data is not described as anonymous.

The study information must identify eligibility, purposes, duration, researcher contact, risks, retention and withdrawal/deletion terms, including whether future model training and product improvement are permitted. These terms have not been invented or approved by the app.

Turn sharing off in Settings → Privacy & Research to cancel pending local deliveries and revoke consent on the server. Offline withdrawals wait for connectivity and the matching sign-in, and block subsequent uploads from that installation. Other devices cannot learn about an offline withdrawal until synchronization. Data already received is handled under the study policy.

Research deletion and retention

Request research-data deletion in Settings → Privacy & Research. The service stops uploads and deletes hosted recordings, and leaves a private request for the researcher to review downloaded copies, backups and training datasets. Account deletion also initiates this process. Local recordings remain separate. Minimal request and consent records may remain under the approved policy; they are not automatically anonymous. Removing recordings does not automatically remove their influence from trained models.

The institution-approved retention period, responsible researcher and private contact details must be added before recruitment and publication. No indefinite retention or arbitrary deletion period is promised by this draft.

Limitations

FocusFix is an experimental activity tool, not a medical device or a validated fatigue or productivity detector. No analytics scripts, cookies or forms are included in this static website. A future hosting provider may process normal web request logs; its details must be added before publication.

Support and source

For recording problems, first inspect the visible Recording/Paused/Idle/Permission needed state. Pause recording or Quit when you want capture stopped; closing a window is different. Check Input Monitoring explicitly in macOS Settings. Local builds have not completed signed-device qualification. Never upload recordings to public support issues. Group Work scores may differ from new local declared work because correction-compatible sync is not yet released.

For general help, use FocusFix support on GitHub. Issues are public: do not post recordings, credentials or personal information. A GitHub account is needed to open an issue.

The app source is available under GPL-3.0-only in the FocusFix app repository. A future website download will include access to its matching source and license.

Preparation date: November 2, 2026. This information still needs release review.
